feedback.title: Record workflow feedback
feedback.imperative: Before committing, reflect honestly on how this run actually went: how closely you followed the skills, handoffs, and checklists; where you had to improvise or work around the instructions; what was ambiguous, missing, or contradictory; and what would have helped. Include the crew Workflow Feedback harvested at each gN-integrate. A 'none' answer requires a run-specific reason ('none — confirmed after review: <what you checked>'); bare 'none' entries fail the invariant check. Append one dated entry for this work-id to .agent-work/AGENT_FEEDBACK.md (create it from templates/AGENT_FEEDBACK.template.md if absent — prefer the project copy under .agent-work/templates/, fall back to the bundled workbench template). This log persists across runs and is never archived with the work-id. Adjudicate each lesson before banking it — the playbook holds open problems you are carrying forward, not a log of everything learned. If a lesson is understood and fixable now, APPLY it this run (make the bounded edit, record it in AGENT_FEEDBACK) and do not add a playbook entry at all; a lesson goes in the bank (an add) ONLY because it needs to be re-observed to be understood, and every add must carry a bank_reason saying what re-observation will clarify. Applying to project doctrine (a docs/agents/* delta or a template working copy — any .md / .template.*) is a human call: it needs authority=human on the apply op, and in delegated/autonomous mode you do NOT self-apply doctrine — surface it to your principal (who may rule 'apply', or 'wait, observe it again') and defer with 'needs human' until they do. Applying a code target (with its test suite as proof) stays autonomous. Then distill what remains into the playbook: write structured delta ops (add [with bank_reason]/confirm/disconfirm/mention/retire/apply/defer — every add/confirm/disconfirm cites a grounding artifact line; corroborate with engine telemetry like rework counts, BLOCK verdicts, waives where possible) to .agent-work/300/lessons-delta.json with tick=true, and apply deterministically: python C:/Programs/constellation-skills-wt/298-300/scripts/apply_lessons_delta.py .agent-work/300/lessons-delta.json --file .agent-work/LESSONS.md. Never edit LESSONS.md directly; if there are no lesson candidates, still apply a tick-only delta. Then settle every threshold-ripe lesson (python C:/Programs/constellation-skills-wt/298-300/scripts/apply_lessons_delta.py --ripe --file .agent-work/LESSONS.md): for each, APPLY it (make the bounded edit to its target — a thin docs/agents/* delta or a project template working copy — confirmed by the human, then an apply op deletes it as paid), or for a constellation lesson EXPORT it (append to .agent-work/CONSTELLATION_FEEDBACK.md — carry the originating lesson id in that entry's Lesson field so the upstream sweep groups recurrences on stable identity, rewording a recurring finding via amend not a new slug — then an export op marks it exported and pinned), or RESOLVE it if you can confirm the upstream fix has already shipped (a resolve op citing the shipping PR/commit marks the constellation lesson fixed-upstream: no longer ripe, immune to re-confirmation, and it ages out of the playbook — this is how an already-fixed defect stops being re-exported every run), or DEFER it with a reason (a broad or contradictory doctrine shift routes to a Charter refresh; an autonomous run without that latitude defers 'needs human'). Lessons flagged charter-review go to a Charter refresh. Then run the feedback invariant check before advancing: python C:/Programs/constellation-skills-wt/298-300/scripts/verify_agent_feedback.py 300 --phase feedback.
